# Why a video teaches: findings behind the lesson rules

The lesson rules (`skills/oldguy/references/teaching.md`, checked by `oldguy lesson`) come from a review of three
videos by four reviewers: a cognitive psychologist, an instructional designer, a perception psychologist, and a
first-time viewer who thought aloud while watching.

| Video | What it is | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| A: job explainer | the silent reference that inspired oldguy | 6–7/10; about 75% of the flow stuck with the viewer |
| B: template engine | an oldguy video about planned work, with a caption band | 3–4/10; about 40% stuck: "I can list the parts, but I can't trace one thing through them" |
| C: appeal drafter | an earlier oldguy video | clear to its owner |

## What made A and C work

- One concrete thing followed through lanes that stay put ("a lawyer clicks Run analysis"; "one box, start to finish").
- Each chapter's map is drawn empty first, then fills; steps pile up and stay lit, so a lost viewer catches up.
- The same visual language in every chapter.
- A reason after each step ("so a forgotten job fails loudly at boot"), and a one-line recap.
- Labels on screen, not the narration.
- Planned work stated once.

## What sank B

- A new kind of picture per chapter, and boxes whose text was replaced every sentence.
- A caption band repeating every spoken word, competing with the diagram for the eyes.
- A new idea every 5.5 s with no pause of a second or more in 166 s.
- Terms used before they were taught, no "so what", no recap.
- A "planned" badge on almost every frame.
- A storyboard rule that banned connecting chapters, which removed the thread between them.

Pauses matter less than structure: C has no pause of a second or more either and still teaches. They were still
added (explainer speaks at 0.9 with 700 ms after each sentence, 1.4 s after a "So" line and at the chapter end),
because a finished thought needs a moment to land.

## Still to build

- The player stops at each chapter's end on its recap, with replay and next.
- Clicking a step jumps to that moment and its code.
- An explorable map after the video, not instead of it.
